newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel urges retail electricity deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel urges retail electricity deregulation.

text.p: Retail electricity sales in Japan, currently monopolised by 10 regional power firms, should be considered for deregulation, a governmental panel said.
Opening up the retail electricity business to independent power producers was suggested in a preliminary report on deregulation by a sub-committee of the Administrative Reform Committee.

The report, issued on Thursday, listed both pros and cons of possible deregulation and also suggested allowing independent power producers to use existing power grids to send electricity in order to enable the new players to break into the retail business.

The cost of building new power grids from scratch would make it prohibitive for new power producers to participate in electricity sales at the retail level, according to one opinion mentioned in the report.
The sub-committee is scheduled to finalise its report by the end of this year after further discussion.
